chunks: And with the preceding chain of narration, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Bakr ibn Salih who said:

My son-in-law wrote to Abu Ja’far the Second, peace be upon him, that: "My father is a Nasibi with wretched views. And I have experienced hardship and pressure from him. I request your opinion, may I be your ransom, regarding supplication for me, and what do you think, may I be your ransom? Do you think I should confront him openly or comply with his whims?"

He, peace be upon him, wrote back: "I have understood your letter and what you have mentioned about your father. God willing, I shall never cease supplicating for you. Compliance is better for you than open confrontation. And with hardship comes ease. So be patient, for the end result is for the God-conscious. May Allah keep you firm on the authority of those whom you have accepted. You and we are all entrusted in the care of Allah, and with Him no trust is ever lost."
Bakr said: Then Allah caused a change of heart in his father toward him, so that he became fully compliant and would not oppose him in anything.

key_terms.المداراة: Mudarat — compliance, tactful accommodation, avoiding open conflict with adversaries
key_terms.ناصب: Nasibi — one who harbors hostility toward the Ahlul Bayt (the Prophet’s family)
key_terms.وديعة: Trust, something entrusted to safekeeping — here meaning divine protection

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Taqi advise about dealing with a hostile Nasibi father?
ai.summary: In this epistolary narrative from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Bakr ibn Salih recounts how his son-in-law wrote to Imam Abu Ja’far the Second (Imam Muhammad al-Taqi, the 9th Imam) seeking guidance about dealing with his Nasibi father who held hostile views toward Ahlul Bayt. The Imam counseled patience and compliance (mudarat) over confrontation, quoting Quran 94:5-6 (‘with hardship comes ease’) and 7:128 (‘the end result is for the God-conscious’). He assured the man of his prayers and placed them both in Allah’s trust. The story concludes with the remarkable outcome: Allah changed the father’s heart so completely that he became fully compliant to his son.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 20. And with the preceding chains of narration, from ‘Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Bakr ibn Swaleh who said:

My son-in-law wrote to Abu Ja’far the second Imam Muhammad Taqi (as), peace be upon him, that: "My father is a Nasibi and has wretched views about Ahlul Bayt. And I have experienced a lot of hardship and pressure from him. I write to request for special prayers for me, may I be your ransom, and to advise me what should be my line of action. Should I confront him or comply with his whims?"

He, peace be upon him, wrote back: "I have understood your letter and what you have mentioned about your father. God willing, I shall never forget you in my prayers. And it is better to be compliant rather than resorting to open confrontation. For with every hardship, there is ease. Be patient, for the end result is always in favour of those who are mindful of duties towards Allah. May Allah keep you firm on the path of those who you have accepted as the authority. You and we are all entrusted in the care of Allah, and with Him, no trust is lost!"
Bakr said: Then Allah caused a change of heart in his father, so that he in turn became compliant to the son.
